transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-30 10:00 PT | Duration: ~52m | Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/rec/ff-20250930-8423
Attendees (as listed): Naomi Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Morales (Redwood DX), Maya Gomez (Sapphire Head of Platform), Jordan Lee (Sapphire Sr Eng), Priya Anand (Sapphire Security), Omar Bashir (Sapphire ML)

Summary (auto-gen): quickstart + auth -> demo of SDK flows, Console walk-through showing route-level cost/latency, Optimize suggestions for batching + prefix cache. Security discussion re: KMS and VPC. Next: perf baseline and pricing follow-up.

[00:00] Naomi: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to walk through a fast codeflow so you can get an idea of how a POC would look. Derek is going to show the SDKs and then we'll jump to Console and Optimize.
[00:18] Derek: cool, i'll share my screen — quick note, i'll use python for the first example and then a tiny TS snippet. our pip package is redwood-inference in the examples, npm package is @redwood/inference in the demo repo, but the api surface is the same.
[00:40] Jordan: quick question before you start — are we going hosted or dedicated for the POC? latency is pretty important for us.
[00:47] Naomi: good Q. we usually recommend hosted for fast onboarding, dedicated for stable committed throughput. we can show both: hosted for the quickstart, and then a dedicated baseline later.
[01:05] Derek: ok code — python example: from redwood_inference import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) — sorry i said REDWOOD_API_KEY, some older docs used RW_API_KEY so watch the env name.
[01:28] Maya: oof, that naming inconsistency bites — good to call it out.
[01:35] Derek: yeah, we'll send the canonical quickstart repo. for typescript: import {RedwoodClient} from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY});
[01:59] Omar: do you have an example for streaming token by token in JS?
[02:06] Derek: yep — i showed a tiny stream handler — we also demoed it in the repo. note: streaming behavior slightly differs between hosted and dedicated if you enable continuous batching — you might see micro-buffering.
[02:35] Priya: security — what about keys and rotation? do you support scoped keys?
[02:43] Naomi: yes we support API keys with scopes and expirations, and we integrate with KMS/HSM for private deployments. for hosted we store keys encrypted; you can rotate via Console.
[03:03] Priya: and audit logs?
[03:06] Luis: Console has token-level audit and per-route tracing, we can export to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
[03:18] Jordan: walk me through env config for a local dev vs prod setup.
[03:22] Derek: local dev — set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ENV=dev, don't commit secrets; we recommend using your secrets manager CI inject. for prod we recommend using the private deployment with KMS keys and VPC peering if you need egress controls.
[03:50] Maya: is there a docker example?
[03:53] Luis: yes, the quickstart has a dockerfile. we also show how to mount credentials from your secret store rather than env vars.
[04:15] Derek: switching to Console — Naomi — i'll pass to you.
[04:19] Naomi: Console view: routes page lets you pin model versions, set rollouts (canary/percentage) and attach Optimize profiles that suggest batching and cache TTLs. in the demo i made a route for "product-recs" and pinned to gptx-1-7b-quant.
[04:45] Jordan: how granular is routing by region? can we route EU traffic to eu models?
[04:49] Naomi: yes, routing rules support region, cost tier, and fallback chains — helpful if you want eu residency and a fallback to hosted us-east for spillover.
[05:10] Omar: Optimize — what metrics does it suggest on?
[05:13] Derek: Optimize looks at latency distributions, token cost, and request size histograms. it will recommend batching window sizes and prefix cache settings. e.g., for a short prompt storefront scenario Optimize suggested 16ms batching with prefix cache enabled to shave ~18% token cost.
[05:42] Jordan: can Optimize recommend quantization profiles?
[05:45] Derek: it will recommend model variants and quantization when it sees you can hit SLOs with a smaller model. we'll run a quick baseline to confirm quality metrics.
[06:05] Priya: if you use shared hosted, is customer data logged with models? compliance wise we need to know retention and opt-out.
[06:12] Naomi: hosted has a configurable retention window; by default ephemeral short-term logs for monitoring, but enterprise contracts can opt-out of retention and use Private with no telemetry. we'll send exact doc links.
[06:28] Maya: in the quickstart can we use a mock dataset to verify latencies before giving real traffic?
[06:33] Derek: yes we included a sample bench harness. we'll run it against your sample prompts — we asked Maya to share the 3 prompts after the call.
[06:50] Jordan: any gotchas with npm vs pip?
[06:53] Luis: only small API naming differences, but behavior identical. watch streaming signatures in older node versions; we have a polyfill in the repo.
[07:06] Naomi: price talk: we'll send hosted per-token and a dedicated monthly commit sheet. for dedicated we can price reserve pools with burst capacity.
[07:18] Maya: our procurement will want contract examples and a template SOW.
[07:22] Naomi: yes we'll include a pilot SOW template.
[07:30] Derek: live code snippet: i ran the sample call — response time ~72ms p50 on hosted for a 120-token prompt. with quantized model on dedicated we expect lower p95 but we'll confirm.
[08:01] Jordan: so the plan is: you run baseline with our sample prompts, show dedicated vs hosted numbers, security sends KMS questions.
[08:10] Naomi: correct. Priya, do you need any infra diagrams?
[08:14] Priya: yes a simple network diagram showing VPC peering and KMS flow would help.
[08:19] Luis: we'll attach that to the follow-up pack.
[08:25] Maya: what about fallback behavior if a model instance is saturated?
[08:29] Derek: Console routing can fallback to a compatible smaller model, or to a CPU-safe path for short bursts. we also expose retry/backoff policies on the SDK.
[08:45] Omar: is cold-start a concern on dedicated?
[08:47] Derek: less so if you use warm pools; Dedicated has pre-warmed lanes and autoscale settings. for startup we recommend a small warm target.
[09:02] Jordan: any integrations with our observability stack?
[09:05] Luis: yes — tracing hooks, and you can push token-level cost to prometheus/grafana via our agent.
[09:20] Naomi: ok quick demo of Optimize UI — shows cost delta if you enable KV cache and change batch size, it simulates token cost savings and estimates latency impact.
[09:42] Maya: curious — do you do privacy preserving caching? like hashing prompts?
[09:46] Derek: yes we can mask or hash identifiers before caching, and you control cache TTLs.
[09:55] Jordan: what about model evals — how do you ensure quality after quantization?
[09:59] Derek: our eval harness runs reference prompt sets and flags regressions. we can run human in the loop checks for high-risk flows.
[10:15] Priya: send SOC2 docs please.
[10:17] Naomi: will do.
[10:23] [minor cross talk] Jordan: sounds good.
[10:35] Derek: i'll summarize the perf plan — run baseline on hosted, then run quantized variant on dedicated with same prompt set. expect to share a spreadsheet with p50/p95 and token cost.
[10:55] Naomi: next steps recap: send quickstart repo, pricing sheets, SOW template, SOC2/KMS network diagram; Derek to run perf baseline.
[11:10] Maya: thanks all, schedule a follow-up next week?
[11:13] Naomi: i'll propose times. thanks everyone.

End of transcript (auto-trimmed).
